verdict: 2026-07-29 09:54:22 PDT — Not sound as sketched. Observing `postMessage` outcomes, sharing close→reopen, edge-triggering logs, and avoiding a new runtime dependency are appropriate and consistent with this repository. I would keep that core, but first make recovery respect manual Hide, make the retry reducer own its complete transition state, and reconcile the impossible App-test/scope combination.

findings.title: The required App tests cannot be built within the declared scope
findings.claim: The test notes require rendered Vitest/jsdom interaction tests, but the repository has no jsdom, happy-dom, Testing Library, or react-test-renderer dependency; its established convention is pure Node-testable orchestrators. AC6 also excludes `client/src/App.test.js`, `client/package.json`, and `package-lock.json`. The proposed tests therefore require either violating scope/no-new-dependency or hand-rolling a DOM harness.
findings.alternative: Follow the repository's existing extraction convention: put the post-failure and best-effort-stop orchestration behind pure injected-dependency functions, test them in `overlayRecover.test.js`, and inspect the hook-free `PresenterControls` element tree for the button state if needed. Amend the test notes to remove the jsdom requirement. If a rendered integration test is mandatory, explicitly add App.test.js and the standard DOM-testing dependencies to scope instead.
findings.win: Makes the gate implementable without an undeclared dependency or forbidden files and reuses the repository's established Node-only test seam.

findings.title: The recovery guard does not preserve a concurrent manual Hide
findings.claim: `recoveringRef` only prevents the two automatic triggers from overlapping. If a rebuild has passed its initial overlay-on check and the presenter clicks Hide while its asynchronous close→start sequence is in flight, Hide can set the UI off and then the older recovery can still call `startCameraOverlay` and `postOverlay`, leaving the camera overlay running while the button says “Show cost on video.” Additionally, `try/finally` updates state but preserves the close rejection, so the click handler still produces an unhandled rejected promise rather than a genuinely best-effort stop.
findings.alternative: Make Hide record intent immediately (`overlayOnRef.current = false` and state off) before awaiting a caught best-effort close. Put the shared single-flight guard inside `rebuildOverlay`, pass it a `getOverlayOn`/generation check, and re-check intent after close and before start/post; an invalidated recovery exits without reopening.
findings.win: Eliminates both the hidden-state/actual-overlay divergence and the unhandled rejection while centralizing concurrency protection for both automatic recovery paths.

findings.title: The proposed reducer owns only half of the cooldown transition
findings.claim: `reducePostResult` receives `lastRebuildAt` but does not return it; App imperatively stamps it afterward. The stated “crosses the threshold and cooldown has elapsed” rule is also incomplete: if the count crosses N during cooldown, later failures no longer cross N, so a literal implementation never retries when cooldown expires. Using `>= N` would work, but contradicts the stated crossing semantics and still leaves one transition split between the reducer and App.
findings.alternative: Have the reducer return the complete next state, including `lastRebuildAt`, plus the effect signal. Define eligibility as `nextFailures >= N && now - lastRebuildAt >= cooldown`; when eligible, return `rebuild: true` and atomically advance `lastRebuildAt` (with an explicit decision on whether the count resets). A success resets only the failure count.
findings.win: Centralizes the retry invariant in one pure transition, removes App's timestamp bookkeeping, and guarantees persistent failures retry at the cooldown cadence instead of potentially stalling forever.
